tier_rationale: The manufacturer's own specification sheet lists the projector's complete interface set as two HDMI ports, a USB Type-A port (power/PC-free playback), a USB Type-B port (USB Plug 'n Play from a computer), and a 3.5mm audio output — no Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Ethernet, or wireless module of any kind, and no smart-TV operating system. The USB-A port can power an external streaming stick (Fire TV, Apple TV, Roku, Chromecast), and Epson's own footnote on that feature specifies the *stick* needs its own wireless network connection — the projector itself contributes only power over USB, not a radio. No FCC ID search turned up an intentional-radiator grant for this model, consistent with Epson filing grants under other product lines (grantee codes D3F, BKM) when they do add radios.
the_unplug_test: Nothing changes, because this projector never had a network connection to lose. It takes HDMI in from a cable box, Blu-ray player, laptop or game console, and projects it — controlled entirely by its included infrared remote. The USB-A port will power a Fire TV Stick or Roku plugged into it, but that stick is a separate smart device with its own account and its own Wi-Fi; the projector itself has no wireless radio, no app, and nothing to phone home with.

repairability.notes: Standard replaceable-lamp architecture (Genuine Epson lamp part number listed on prior-generation sibling's spec sheet); lamp and air filter are consumer-replaceable parts sold directly by Epson.

sources.supports: Manufacturer specification sheet: full interface list (2x HDMI, USB-A, USB-B, 3.5mm audio out) with no wireless interface listed; footnote clarifies the USB-A streaming-stick power feature requires the stick's own wireless network connection, not one built into the projector.
Manufacturer product page confirms current in-stock status, price ($749.99, reduced from $849.99), and the same interface set with no Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/app/account mentioned anywhere on the page.

Sibling control: Seiko Epson Corporation's grantee codes (D3F, BKM) show the company does file FCC intentional-radiator grants for products that contain radios (e.g. its Wi-Fi-equipped streaming projectors), making the absence of any grant found for the Home Cinema 980 meaningful rather than an artifact of a vendor that never files.

open_questions: Did not locate a specific FCC ID search result confirming zero intentional-radiator filings under model number V11HB63020 directly on fccid.io (searched the grantee's filing list rather than the model number itself); the manufacturer's own spec sheet is treated as the primary source for the no-radio claim, with the grantee search as corroborating sibling control.
Did not verify repairability/parts availability specifically for this model; the note reflects the standard Epson Home Cinema lamp-projector service pattern rather than a HC980-specific source.
notes: Fills the empty 'projector' subcategory. Distinguish from Epson's own Home Cinema streaming-series projectors (e.g. HC2350/LS650), which bundle a bult-in Android TV/Chromecast streaming media player with Wi-Fi and would be a different tier; the plain Home Cinema numbered line (880 before it, 980 now) has no smart platform and is sold alongside the streaming line with no naming overlap.
